A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L4Q research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Matching content across layout changes and table redistribution supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original CSQA and MMLU evaluations, memory and throughput measurements, and initialization and hyperparameter experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and adds LLaMA-3 8B CSQA evaluations in Tables 2–3 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The weight-and-LoRA merging procedure, quantization, gradient computation, and quantization initialization remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A–B. The added adapter-initialization description does not establish a change to the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Stanford-Alpaca and evaluate the same seven CSQA tasks and MMLU coverage. The added LLaMA-3 8B results extend model configurations without introducing different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. The new LLaMA-3 rows use the existing pre-trained, LoRA, GPTQ, OmniQuant, LoftQ*, QLoRA*, QA-LoRA, and QAT-LoRA comparisons. Initialization and efficiency comparator sets are also retained.

E3.justification: v6 adds LLaMA-3 8B to the evaluated model configurations at 4-bit and 3-bit precision (Tables 2–3 and 13a). The stated splits, metrics, ranks, quantization groups, and training budgets for existing experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The initialization comparison, rank and group-size ablations, convergence analysis, and efficiency analyses are unchanged (Figure 3, Tables 4–8, Figure 5, and Appendices E–F). The added model scores do not introduce a separate robustness or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the evaluations. The added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v6 adds aggregate and per-task LLaMA-3 8B CSQA results (Tables 2–3 and 13a). L4Q scores 66.8% at 4-bit and 63.5% at 3-bit; the corresponding QAT-LoRA scores are 65.7% and 63.1%. These are new-model results, while previously reported numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–38, including the quantization definitions, STE-based gradient derivations, and initialization formulas, are unchanged. Appendices A–B introduce no new assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about integrating QAT with LoRA, reducing training memory, and preserving accuracy and inference efficiency. The additional model results support existing contributions.

C2.justification: Limitations drops specific proposed memory benefits of activation quantization and efficiency and low-resource benefits of improved LoRA initialization, while retaining the broader future-work directions. Ethical Considerations also removes the explicit statement that potential harms and biases are not examined further.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies Kaiming-uniform initialization for adapter A and zero initialization for B. This is additional disclosure, without evidence of changed initialization. The head-precision clarification largely repeats Appendix F; existing hardware, hyperparameter tables, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to QAT, PTQ, and quantization-aware PEFT remain unchanged. The added model results do not introduce new related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v6 makes localized prose edits, expands setup explanations, and shortens the limitations and ethics sections. It also revises author and correspondence presentation, adds acknowledgments, and inserts an Appendix heading. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain LLaMA-3 rows, and Table 13a gains its detailed block, moving the existing LLaMA-1 13B block to Table 13b. Figure 3 and Table 1 change column placement, with associated layout shifts. The figures themselves retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added LLaMA-3 comparisons and per-task scores provide limited additional validation across base models, while explicit adapter initialization improves reproducibility. Existing evidence is retained. These gains are modest: Table 9 still lacks LLaMA-3-specific learning rates, and the shortened limitations and ethics discussion loses some specificity.
